nodes.text: A child growing up through care services or adoption needs people who know them, a secure place in the world and reasons to look forward to adult life. Improving child welfare involves the ordinary experience of being listened to, enjoying childhood, discovering interests and finding people who help those interests grow. It also involves the society that will receive the young adult.

nodes.text: A Protopian Gambit means a deliberate first move towards a better future that also improves something now. The move produces experience, exposes mistakes and leaves people with more informed choices for what follows. In child welfare, that first move might be a small supported programme where a young person completes a project, understands a relevant rule and meets a mentor who continues to help. [P4-P5]

nodes.text: Understanding the change in intelligence

nodes.text: Artificial intelligence is software that performs tasks such as interpreting language, finding patterns, generating media or proposing actions. Current systems work across an expanding range of tasks, although performance remains uneven. An impressive explanation may contain a false detail; a successful demonstration may fail in a different setting. The International AI Safety Report 2026 describes both improving capability and substantial uncertainty about its trajectory. [S1]

nodes.text: Consider a fictional twelve-year-old, Alex, who enjoys making small games. Alex chooses to build a garden scene where a player looks after plants.
